I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou pattern: winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10 mu. I would not switch to something complicated this year. I am 63, so I want a system I know well, can manage on time, and can still get stable grain from. In Quzhou, this wheat-maize rotation is still the main road, and recent local work in 曲周科技小院 and Ministry of Agriculture guidance keeps pointing the same way: balance nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium, save water, sow wheat a bit later in autumn, and use improved seed and tighter field management for maize and wheat. So I will finish this standing winter wheat with steady water and disease control, harvest it in June, then direct-seed summer maize quickly after harvest, keep fertilizer moderate rather than excessive, and rely on a few key irrigation and spray timings instead of many passes. Sources I used: China Agricultural University Quzhou station on Quzhou wheat-maize rotation and local “吨半粮” results ([1](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/col/col46309/index.html), [2](https://qzsyz.cau.edu.cn/art/2024/10/8/art_46317_1039835.html)); Ministry of Agriculture guidance for Huang-Huai-Hai wheat and maize ([3](https://www.moa.gov.cn/gk/nszd_1/nszd_2/202409/t20240924_6463166.htm), [4](https://www.moa.gov.cn/ztzl/2022sxjxs/nszd/202206/t20220601_6401266.htm), [5](https://nyncj.chengde.gov.cn/art/2012/7/9/art_667_93731.html)).
